title: BatchEnsemble rank-one logical experts vs Mirror views
hypothesis: Input-side Givens Mirror views represent aligned routed expert functions at fewer bytes than BatchEnsemble rank-one factors; arbitrary experts need private parameters.
mirror_coordinate: Four per-role input Givens angle vectors

development.selection_metric: routed MSE and actual payload bytes

optimization.representation_fit: scipy nonlinear least squares for BatchEnsemble and Mirror; pooled least squares for tied

storage.serializer: uncompressed NumPy NPZ retaining fitted dtype

compute.active_compute_proxy: routed dense output MACs; decode cost separately disclosed

success_gate: At least 3/4 fresh aligned worlds: Mirror MSE <=1.10x independent, <=80% independent bytes, fewer bytes than BatchEnsemble.
failure_gate: Mirror aligned MSE >1.25x independent on >=3/4 worlds or more bytes than independent without quality gain.
protocol_variant_note: A separate 1200-update two-expert regression screen is retained under protocol_variants/fixed_update_failure and failed at development; its results are not pooled.
reconciliation: Literal frozen relative-MSE criterion recomputed from raw fresh rows passes 1/4, not the source report claim of 4/4; a separate fixed-update protocol failed at development.
